The bug comes from the `ordering_parts` regex on `SQLCompiler`. Without `re.MULTILINE | re.DOTALL`, `^(.*)\s(?:ASC|DESC).*` only matched the last line of a multiline RawSQL clause. `get_order_by()` then took `without_ordering` from that last line and added it to `seen`. Two clauses with identical last lines were treated as duplicates, so the second was dropped. The current code already has the fix: the regex is compiled with `re.MULTILINE | re.DOTALL`, so `(.*)` captures the whole SQL before the final ASC/DESC. The duplicate check is at compiler.py:501, `without_ordering = self.ordering_parts.search(sql)[1]`.

Media.merge (static method) in django/forms/widgets.py, together with Media.__add__, which now keeps the lists unmerged. Together they fix the bug. __add__ just concatenates _js_lists/_css_lists, and merge resolves all the lists at once with a TopologicalSorter, so the intermediate ColorPicker+SimpleText merge no longer imposes a false order constraint. The MediaOrderConflictWarning is raised only on a real CycleError.

HttpResponseBase.make_bytes handles memoryview by converting it with bytes(value), so HttpResponse(memoryview(b"My Content")).content gives b'My Content'. The content setter also treats memoryview like bytes and doesn't iterate over it.

The fix is in iter_modules_and_files in django/utils/autoreload.py. It wraps path.exists() in try/except ValueError, because network filesystems can return null bytes in file paths. It logs the error at debug level and skips that path with continue, so path.resolve() is never called on it. I didn't run it or try to reproduce the error.

The models.E028 check lives in check_all_models in django/core/checks/model_checks.py. It collects every managed, non-proxy model's db_table, then reports any table used by more than one model. If that is longer than max_length, it returns the error fields.E009: "'max_length' is too small to fit the longest value in 'choices' (%d characters)." The comparison and the error are at line 371.

parse_http_date handles two-digit years relative to the current year. It takes the current century. If the two-digit year is more than 50 above the current year's last two digits, it moves the date back one century. This replaces the old hard-coded 0-69 → 2000s and 70-99 → 1900s rule. The check is `if year - (current_year % 100) > 50:` in django/utils/http.py.
The check is in `IsNull.as_sql` in `django/db/models/lookups.py`. If `self.rhs` is not a `bool`, it raises `ValueError("The QuerySet value for an isnull lookup must be True or False.")`.

MigrationAutodetector.generate_altered_fields in django/db/migrations/autodetector.py handles ForeignKey to_field renames: if (rename_key + (remote_field_name,)) is in self.renamed_fields, it repoints new_field.remote_field.model and field_name to the old field's values (so to_field comparison/deconstruction accounts for the renamed target field).
The fix is `Choices.__str__` in django/db/models/enums.py. It returns `str(self.value)`, so `str()` on a TextChoices or IntegerChoices member gives "first" instead of "MyChoice.FIRST_CHOICE".

The fix is already in `Field.contribute_to_class()`. It only sets the default `get_FOO_display` if the model class doesn't define one in its own `__dict__`: `if "get_%s_display" % self.name not in cls.__dict__:`. Before this check, the field overwrote a user-defined `get_FOO_display()` in 2.2+.

The "database is locked" error comes from `DatabaseCreation.test_db_signature()` in the SQLite backend. I haven't run the tests. I'm going from the code and from my memory of the upstream Django fix.

The signature is what `django/test/utils.py` (`setup_databases`) uses to decide whether two aliases share one test database. When the test database is on disk, the old code built the signature from `settings_dict["NAME"]` alone. In the settings in the report, `default` and `other` have the same `NAME`, so they got the same signature. Django then treated `other` as a mirror of `default` instead of creating its own test database. The test `admin_views.test_multidb` then wrote to both aliases and hit the lock. The `TEST["NAME"]` files from the report are never part of the signature in that case.

The code in the workspace already has the fix. The `else` branch at line 127 appends the test database name, so each file-backed test database gets its own signature. In-memory databases still use the alias, as before.

I only read the code and didn't run `admin_views.test_multidb` against it.

Field.deconstruct() builds the field's import path from `__class__.__qualname__` instead of `__name__`. This is why an inner class serializes as `Outer.Inner` rather than `Inner`. The base `Field.deconstruct` sets `path = "%s.%s" % (self.__class__.__module__, self.__class__.__qualname__)`. A second line with the same expression, at 639, is in the same file. I didn't open that one.

The crash comes from `RegexPattern.match` in `django/urls/resolvers.py`. This copy already has the fix. When a pattern has named groups, `args = () if kwargs else match.groups()` (line 206) stops the unnamed groups from being passed as positional arguments. Your pattern has an unnamed inner group, `(html|json|xml)`, nested inside the named group `format`. Before the fix, that inner group was passed positionally in addition to the keyword argument, which produced the "3 were given" TypeError. Line 207 also drops named groups that didn't match (value `None`), so the view's default `format='html'` applies.

Fixed in Field.contribute_to_class: it now only skips adding get_FOO_display() when the method is defined explicitly in the class's own __dict__ (`"get_%s_display" % self.name not in cls.__dict__`). Before, it used hasattr, so the inherited method blocked the child's field from installing its own. A child that overrides the choices now gets a get_FOO_display() bound to its own field.

The E004 check is `check_language_settings_consistent`. It calls `get_supported_language_variant(settings.LANGUAGE_CODE)` and returns E004 only if that raises LookupError. `get_supported_language_variant` tries the base language ("de" for "de-at") before it gives up, so a sublanguage with an available base language should no longer trigger E004. In Django 3.0, `GROUP BY "status"` comes from grouping by the annotation alias instead of the subquery expression. In this checkout, `Query.set_group_by` does that at `query.py:2253`. When `allow_aliases` is true and the annotation has no aggregate, it appends `Ref(alias, annotation)`. The compiler then emits that as `GROUP BY "status"`. That name is ambiguous because the joined `test_app_ab` table also has a `status` column. I found this by reading the code. I did not run the query or check how the compiler renders the `Ref`.

SafeExceptionReporterFilter.cleanse_setting() in django/views/debug.py only recursed into dicts and returned other iterables unchanged. This copy of the code already handles lists and tuples. It recurses into them by calling cleanse_setting("", v) on each item, so the sensitive keys of dicts nested in lists are cleansed too. The list branch is at line 136 and the tuple branch at line 138.

The crash comes from `_delete_composed_index()` in `django/db/backends/base/schema.py`. It raises `ValueError("Found wrong number (%s) of constraints ...")` whenever the number of matching constraints isn't exactly 1. When index_together and unique_together cover the same fields, the lookup can match both the `_uniq` and the `_idx` constraint. In this checkout, `alter_index_together` (line 595 onward) already narrows the lookup by passing `{"index": True, "unique": False}` when it deletes an index. The unique-side deletion at line 573 passes `{"unique": True, "primary_key": False}`. `_delete_composed_index` (line 608) also excludes names from `Meta.constraints` and `Meta.indexes`. If more than one unique constraint matches on a backend that allows several on the same fields, it picks the default `unique_together` name. I read this code but didn't run a migration to confirm the crash is gone.

In Collector.delete() (django/db/models/deletion.py), deleted_counter only records a model label when the count is non-zero (`if count: deleted_counter[qs.model._meta.label] += count` for fast deletes, and the same guard for regular instance deletes), so zero deletions yield (0, {}) consistently for both simple and FK models.

QuerySet.distinct() already raises on combined queries (union/intersection/difference) by calling self._not_support_combined_queries("distinct") at the start of the method.

StaticFilesHandlerMixin.get_response_async, which serves the static file through sync_to_async(self.serve) and turns Http404 into a response with response_for_exception. This is the async response method the question says was missing.

slugify() in django/utils/text.py already strips leading and trailing dashes and underscores. The final line is `return re.sub(r"[-\s]+", "-", value).strip("-_")`, and the docstring says the same. I did not run it.

Query.check_filterable in django/db/models/sql/query.py raises NotSupportedError when the value has `resolve_expression` and `getattr(expression, "filterable", True)` is falsy. A model instance with a `filterable` field set to False meets both conditions, so it is rejected as if it were an unfilterable expression. Model instances have `resolve_expression` only if the model defines it, and the `filterable` field supplies the falsy attribute.

The bug is in `SQLCompiler.find_ordering_name`. For `order_by("record__root_id")`, the condition at line 1054 (`getattr(field, "attname", None) != pieces[-1]`) is meant to skip the related model's default ordering when the field's attname is given. It doesn't skip it here, so `OneModel.Meta.ordering = ("-id",)` is applied. That adds the extra join and the inverted sort. I read this code but did not run the queryset to confirm it.

Query.set_empty() in django/db/models/sql/query.py is what QuerySet.none() calls. It adds a NothingNode to the query's own where clause. It then calls set_empty() on each query in combined_queries, so none() also empties the sub-queries of a union. The compiler (compiler.py:607) drops empty parts of a union and raises EmptyResultSet when no parts are left.

ValidationError.__eq__ is defined in django/core/exceptions.py. It returns NotImplemented if the other object isn't a ValidationError. Otherwise it compares hash(self) == hash(other). __hash__ builds the hash from message, code and params for a single error. For error_dict and error_list, I only saw the start of __hash__, which handles the single-error case, so I did not confirm how it makes the comparison independent of error order.

The `add_item()` call in `Feed.get_feed` (django/contrib/syndication/views.py) passes `comments=self._get_dynamic_attr("item_comments", item)`. That means `item_comments` is already supported directly, without going through `item_extra_kwargs`. The code didn't need a change.

The autodetector already puts AlterOrderWithRespectTo ahead of AddIndex when it creates a new model. In `generate_created_models`, the AlterOrderWithRespectTo operation is added at line 703. The duplicates are avoided in apply_limit_choices_to_to_formfield(). It wraps the limit_choices_to filter in an Exists() subquery instead of filtering the queryset with a join directly. The Exists() call is at line 132, with the comment "Use Exists() to avoid potential duplicates" at line 130.

The fix is in SessionBase.decode(). It now catches any exception raised while decoding session data, including the binascii.Error from the legacy decode path. It returns an empty session instead of crashing. A BadSignature is logged first as "Session data corrupted".

Field.__eq__ in corpus/django/db/models/fields/__init__.py already compares both creation_counter and the field's model, so B's and C's inherited `myfield` compare unequal. The same file's __lt__ orders by creation_counter first and only compares models (app_label, model_name) when the counters tie. __hash__ (line 689) still returns `hash(self.creation_counter)`, so it hasn't been updated. The model class is added to the app_list context by the `"model": model` entry in `model_dict`, built in `AdminSite._build_app_dict` in `corpus/django/contrib/admin/sites.py`. `get_app_list` returns these dicts.

The fix is already in PasswordResetTokenGenerator._make_hash_value(). It gets the email with `user.get_email_field_name()` and falls back to "" if the user has none. It then appends that email to the hash string, so changing the email invalidates any unused reset token.

The fix is already in `resolve_lookup_value` in `django/db/models/sql/query.py`. It checks `hasattr(type_, "_make")` to detect a namedtuple and rebuilds it with `type_(*values)`, so the resolved values are expanded into the constructor. Other tuple and list types still get `type_(values)`.

In ManagementUtility.execute(), the preprocessing CommandParser is created with prog=self.prog_name (plus usage="%(prog)s subcommand [options] [args]", add_help=False, allow_abbrev=False), so %(prog)s uses the program name computed from the passed argv rather than sys.argv[0].

The crash comes from the `exec()` calls in `Command.handle` in `shell.py`. The `-c` command is run through `exec(options["command"], globals())` at line 117. The stdin path at line 127 does the same with `exec(sys.stdin.read(), globals())`.

The version in this corpus already passes `globals()` as the second argument, which looks like the fix for this bug. The original code was `exec(options['command'])` with no namespace argument. Called that way, `exec` runs the code in `handle`'s local scope. A function defined in that code then can't see names imported in the same code, such as `django`, so it raises `NameError`. I did not run anything to confirm this.

Django's own fix passes an empty dict, `exec(options["command"], {})`, so the code gets a fresh global namespace instead of the shell module's globals.

InlineModelAdmin.__init__ in django/contrib/admin/options.py already does this. If verbose_name_plural is None and the inline sets verbose_name, it sets verbose_name_plural to format_lazy("{}s", self.verbose_name). KeyTransformIsNull in django/db/models/fields/json.py: its as_oracle (isnull=True builds "NOT has_key OR lhs IS NULL") and as_sqlite (JSON_TYPE(...) IS NULL) methods are what make __isnull=True also match JSON null on SQLite and Oracle.

Django's `_check_default_pk` in django/db/models/base.py raises models.W042 when `cls._meta.pk.auto_created` is true. The fix for inherited primary keys is the exclusion at lines 1611-1615. ModelChoiceField's default invalid_choice message lacks %(value)s. Change it to "Select a valid choice. %(value)s is not one of the available choices." The ValidationError raised in ModelChoiceField.to_python already passes params={"value": value}.

The fix is in Model._prepare_related_fields_for_save (django/db/models/base.py): the check for re-syncing the related object's pk after assignment uses `getattr(self, field.attname) in field.empty_values` (rather than only `is None`), so an empty-string product_id is refreshed from the now-set pk of the related instance via setattr(self, field.name, obj).

Q._combine in django/db/models/query_utils.py: when self is empty it returns other.copy() (shallow copy via Node.__copy__ in utils/tree.py) instead of deep-copying/pickling the Q's children, so non-pickleable values like dict_keys no longer raise TypeError for Q() | Q(x__in={}.keys()).

The TypeError comes from `Q._combine` in `corpus/django/db/models/query_utils.py`. It used to reject anything that wasn't a `Q` with `if not isinstance(other, Q): raise TypeError(other)`. Here that check is `if getattr(other, "conditional", False) is False: raise TypeError(other)`, which accepts conditional expressions such as `Exists`. So `Q() & Exists(...)` no longer raises. When the `Q` is empty, it returns `other.copy()`. I did not run it to confirm. I also didn't need `__rand__`, because `Q.__and__` handles the pair.

The crash comes from `Expressions.rename_table_references` in `django/db/backends/ddl_references.py`. During `_remake_table`, the unique constraint's expressions are renamed from the old table to the `new__` table. If that step sets a table alias on each `Col`, the SQL is compiled as `"table"."col"` instead of a bare column name. SQLite rejects the `.` operator in index expressions. The current code calls `self.expressions.relabeled_clone({old_table: new_table})` at line 237. I read this code but did not run the repro. I'm inferring from memory that the older 4.0a1 code set `col.alias` directly, and I didn't confirm that here.

The fix belongs in RenameModel.database_forwards (django/db/migrations/operations/models.py). It currently calls schema_editor.alter_db_table() and then alters every related field and M2M table, with no check on whether the table name actually changes. When db_table is set explicitly, old_model._meta.db_table equals new_model._meta.db_table. The base alter_db_table already skips the table rename in that case. However, RenameModel still goes on to alter the related fields, which is where Postgres drops and recreates foreign key constraints. SQLite recreates the table. The fix is an early return in database_forwards when the two db_table values are equal. This is not applied yet.

MultiWidget.id_for_label in django/forms/widgets.py (`def id_for_label(self, id_): return ""`) is the method the issue is about. In this corpus it already returns "" instead of f'{id_}0'. The issue asks to remove the method completely. The ChoiceWidget version at line 718 and the RadioSelect version at line 847 are different widgets.

URLValidator.__call__ now catches the ValueError that urlsplit raises ("Invalid IPv6 URL") and re-raises it as a ValidationError. The code is `except ValueError: raise ValidationError(self.message, code=self.code, params={"value": value})`. forms.URLField.to_python already does the same around its own urlsplit calls. I did not run the failing input.

The crash comes from how `NegatedExpression.as_sql` handles the empty case. `~Q(pk__in=[])` is wrapped in a `NegatedExpression`, and compiling the inner `pk__in=[]` raises `EmptyResultSet`. The `except EmptyResultSet` branch catches this and returns `1=1`, or `Value(True)` on backends that support boolean expressions in SELECT. Without that handling, the wrapper produced no SQL, which is why the query rendered as `SELECT AS "foo"`. The code in this checkout already contains this handling. I read it and did not run the query.

MigrationRecorder.ensure_schema (recorder.py) creates the django_migrations table whenever has_table() is false, without ever consulting router.allow_migrate; record_applied/record_unapplied call it unconditionally and applied_migrations doesn't check the router either.

Subquery.__init__ sets `self.query.subquery = True` after cloning the query. This is the fix the issue asks for. Without the flag, Query.as_sql doesn't wrap the SQL in parentheses, so `Subquery.as_sql` strips the first and last characters with `subquery_sql[1:-1]` (line 1578).

MessageEncoder.default in cookie.py now checks `if obj.extra_tags is not None:` instead of testing truthiness. An empty-string extra_tags is therefore appended to the encoded message and survives the round trip.

The cause is the `template_changed` file_changed receiver. With BASE_DIR in DIRS, every project file sits under a template dir. The receiver then returned True, which tells the autoreloader the change was handled, so it skipped the restart. The fix is the early return for `.py` files, so Python file changes still trigger a restart.

In this code, `SimpleLazyObject` does implement `__radd__`. It is defined in `corpus/django/utils/functional.py` at line 435 as `@new_method_proxy def __radd__(self, other): return other + self`, so the bug report's complaint doesn't apply to this version.

The fix is in `get_conditional_response` in django/utils/cache.py. Line 176 makes it skip an empty If-Modified-Since value, so `parse_http_date_safe` only runs on a non-empty header. The existing code already has this guard, so I didn't change anything. I read the code but didn't run it.

I also checked `was_modified_since` in django/views/static.py. An empty string reaches `parse_http_date`, which should raise `ValueError` that the function catches, so it returns True and nothing raises there either.

RenameIndex.database_backwards in django/db/migrations/operations/models.py returns early as a no-op when old_fields is set (an unnamed index). The index therefore keeps its new name. Re-applying forwards then tries to rename it to the same new name again, and PostgreSQL raises "relation already exists". The fix is to restore the old auto-generated name on backwards instead of returning early.

The autodetector's `_generate_removed_field` adds a `foo_together_change` dependency to the RemoveField operation. This makes the AlterUniqueTogether run before the field is removed. That avoids the "Found wrong number (0) of constraints" error when a FK changes to an M2M. The m2m/concrete switch in `generate_altered_fields` calls this method. I found this by reading the code and did not run it or reproduce the error.

BaseCommand.create_parser sets the default argparse formatter via kwargs.setdefault("formatter_class", DjangoHelpFormatter). DjangoHelpFormatter subclasses HelpFormatter, which collapses whitespace in the help description. A command can pass its own formatter_class (e.g. RawDescriptionHelpFormatter) to create_parser to keep line breaks.

`django.utils.html.json_script` already accepts an `encoder` parameter (`def json_script(value, element_id=None, encoder=None)`), and it passes `encoder or DjangoJSONEncoder` to `json.dumps`. The `json_script` template filter in `defaultfilters.py` still calls it without an encoder argument, so it always uses `DjangoJSONEncoder`.

check_for_template_tags_with_the_same_name collects library paths from both TEMPLATES OPTIONS['libraries'] and get_template_tag_modules() into one dict. The same module path gets registered twice when a custom library points to an installed app's templatetags module. The check only reports a conflict when a name has more than one distinct path. This code already collects the paths in `defaultdict(set)`, so duplicate identical paths collapse into one entry and no longer trigger the "'my_tags' is used for multiple template tag modules: 'someapp.templatetags.my_tags', 'someapp.templatetags.my_tags'" message. I didn't run the check to confirm this.

The crash comes from the select mask using the proxy model's _meta instead of the concrete model's. The fix is already in this code. In `_get_only_select_mask`, the related model is resolved with `field.remote_field.model._meta.concrete_model`, and the recursion uses `related_model._meta`. The defer-mask counterpart (`_get_defer_select_mask`) does the same at lines 746 and 769.

inspectdb already generates related_name for repeated relations to the same model. It keeps a `used_relations` set per table. When a relation's target model is already in that set, it sets `related_name` to "<model_name lowercased>_<att_name>_set". The target is then added to the set.

The fix is already in place in this code. In PostgreSQL's `settings_to_cmd_args_env`, the extra parameters are added with `args.extend(parameters)` before the database name is appended with `args += [dbname]`. That puts the extra options ahead of the dbname, as psql expects.

The warning comes from ManagementForm, which sets no template_name of its own. It renders through the renderer's default form template, which is what triggers the deprecation warning. The fix is to give ManagementForm an explicit template_name, for example "django/forms/div.html", so the warning isn't raised. The template makes no difference to the output, because the form only produces hidden inputs. I did not find that attribute on the class in this corpus, and I did not find the warning-raising code either. This answer rests on reading the class and the renderer defaults. I did not run anything to confirm it.

Already implemented in EnumSerializer.serialize: for enum.Flag values it decomposes the value into member flags (list(self.value) on Python 3.11+, otherwise enum._decompose) and joins them with " | " as `module.Class['NAME']` expressions.

In FormSet.empty_form (django/forms/formsets.py), form_kwargs is built as {**self.get_form_kwargs(None), ..., "empty_permitted": True, "use_required_attribute": False, ...}. Because the user's form_kwargs are spread first, the forced empty_permitted=True overrides any user-supplied empty_permitted, so it is ignored for empty_form.

The null/empty guard in `format()` in `corpus/django/utils/numberformat.py` already covers this. `if number is None or number == "": return mark_safe(number)` returns before `str_number[0]` is reached. The line that raised the IndexError is `if str_number[0] == "-":` at line 72, and it can no longer see an empty string.

UserChangeForm.__init__ in django/contrib/auth/forms.py formats the password help_text link as f"../../{self.instance.pk}/password/" instead of the hardcoded "../password/", so the link no longer breaks when UserAdmin is reached via ?_to_field=uuid.

Model Field.formfield() sets show_hidden_initial=True when the field's default is callable (e.g. ArrayField with default=list). This renders the hidden "initial-..." input that the question points to.
get_latest_lastmod now uses max(..., default=None), so empty sitemaps return None instead of raising ValueError.

The race described in the report is fixed in the current code. `has_key` now opens the file directly and catches `FileNotFoundError`, returning `False` instead of raising if another thread deletes the file between the check and the open.

In create_permissions, the content type lookup was the call that ignored the `database` parameter. It used `ContentType.objects.get_for_model(...)`, which goes through the db router's db_for_read. The code now uses `ContentType.objects.db_manager(using).get_for_model(klass, for_concrete_model=False)`, so the lookup runs on the database passed to migrate. I did not run it.

The wrong object comes from the `local_setter` that `get_related_selections` assigns to a FilteredRelation in `klass_info`. That setter is `partial(local_setter, final_field)`. It caches the joined object on `from_obj` as the reverse relation, whatever the path length. With a multi-level path like `pool__tournament__pool`, `from_obj` isn't the model that owns the final field, so it caches the wrong object. This is why `p[0].pool.tournament` ends up a `PoolStyle`.

This checkout already has the fix. `local_setter` is only used when `len(joins) <= 2`. Longer paths get `local_setter_noop`, defined at line 1308. I haven't run the test case against this code.

The `has_add_permission` check the ticket asks for is already in `show_save_as_new` in `submit_row`. The condition is `not is_popup and has_add_permission and change and save_as`. It has no `has_change_permission` check, which the ticket's own rewrite also includes. I read the code and did not run it or any tests.

AlterField.reduce already handles a following AlterField on the same field. It does this by checking isinstance(operation, (AlterField, RemoveField)) together with is_same_field_operation, then returning [operation]. This is the code the question proposes adding, so no change is needed.

The case is covered in _check_list_display_item in django/contrib/admin/checks.py: a reverse relation such as "choice" (one_to_many / many_to_many) in list_display is rejected by the check at lines 933-944, which emits admin.E109 ("must not be a many-to-many field or a reverse foreign key"). E108 (line 930) is raised only when the item is neither a field nor an attribute.

RenameIndex.reduce in django/db/migrations/operations/models.py — it merges consecutive RenameIndex operations (the old_fields index_together rename followed by another rename) during squashing/optimization.

The `join` filter in django/template/defaultfilters.py only escapes the joining string when `autoescape` is true. When `autoescape` is off, the `else` branch does a plain `arg.join(value)`, so the separator is left unescaped.

In Query._get_only_select_mask, related_model is computed as field.remote_field.model._meta.concrete_model for all relations. For a reverse relation (a OneToOneRel, i.e. field in opts.related_objects) this resolves to the wrong model, so the nested only() mask ('secondary__secondary_field_1') is applied against the wrong opts and the related model's fields aren't restricted. The fix is to use field.related_model._meta.concrete_model in the reverse case (alongside field_key = field.field) and keep field.remote_field.model for forward relations.

In QuerySet._batched_insert (django/db/models/query.py), the condition `if bulk_return and (on_conflict is None or on_conflict == OnConflict.UPDATE)` keeps returning_fields (db_returning_fields) for update_conflicts, so IDs are returned; for ignore_conflicts they are dropped (the else branch calls _insert without returning_fields).

The bug is in FunctionTypeSerializer.serialize in django/db/migrations/serializer.py. For a classmethod, it builds the path from `klass.__name__`. That gives only "Capability" and drops the outer class "Profile". It should use `klass.__qualname__` instead, which produces "appname.models.Profile.Capability.default".
